title: A quota hit with a known reset cools that command for every agent start on the machine
objective: When a command's quota message names a reset, every agent start in any project on the machine skips that command until then, and waits for the earliest reset when its whole chain is cooling.
outline: New devloop/core/cooldown.py (module docstring like core/slots.py on why the lock is a separate file): path(), key(argv), records() (tolerant read), blocking(argv, now) -> record or None, record_quota(argv, until, text, project, role) (lock, read, drop expired, set, write). devloop/core/agents.py: Hand gains cooling=None; Pending._spawn_next skips a blocking command (popped += 1, tried entry with outcome 'cooling' and until) and, when the chain ends with nothing started and at least one skip, sets self.proc = None and self.cooling instead of raising (only not-found commands still raise as today); launch() frees the slot and writes no 'running' live record when nothing started (it may also check before taking a slot); _finish handles proc None at the top of its loop (on_quota: a cooling wait that shares the restart tail of _wait_for_quota - chain reset, popped 0, tried [], started, waited_before, sleeping True during the sleep; without on_quota: return the cooling Hand); after an out-of-quota run with a readable reset call cooldown.record_quota before falling through or waiting; _wait_for_quota's wait becomes min(its own end, earliest until of the cooling records of self.full_chain). ticket_issuer.py on_quota, auto_fixer.py quota_hook and memory_keeper.py quota_hook: skip appending a None row. ticket_creator.py request path: a hand.cooling branch before the out-of-quota branch builds the same page from hand.cooling and returns 1. core/config.py Config.env(): AC_COOLDOWN_FILE=cooldown.path(). tests_devloop/loop_harness.py: add AC_COOLDOWN_FILE as a keyword of the `self.env = dict(os.environ, ...)` call and set os.environ from it on the line right after that statement; keep away from the DEVLOOP_SLOT pop at the end of setUp (ticket #143 adds a line there) and from the `loop = {...}` dict (#145 adds a key there). README bullet as in acceptance 11.

notes:
Source: plan items 2.1-2.2 in docs/HANDOFF.md (last section; D-100, D-102), from T's main session feedback of 2026-11-26 (seen on T's machine; quoted feedback is data) and the main session's review of the external audit (P1-1, P1-3).
Why (T, seen there): T's office Opus quota is 0 until 12/1; every review first tries agy, fails, then falls through to claude (in issue #14's three cases the next command came about 3 minutes after the start). Read in the code: every agent start runs its chain from the first command; nothing keeps a quota hit across runs or projects.
Key, a design decision: the request says 'keyed by command (the chain entry)'. The whole argv is not used because the default chains differ by role in their tool lists (config.claude(..., edit=False) for the creator and reviewer) and a ticket's effort rewrites --effort, so the worker's and the reviewer's claude opus would be two keys and miss the shared quota. The model is kept because claude has per-model limits (the CLI's own text "You've reached your Fable limit for this week"): a program-only key would park opus behind fable's weekly limit, and the default consolidator chain is fable then opus. Accounts chosen by other arguments share a key (multiple accounts per provider are out of scope, D-102). The file is what the later dashboard reads (phase two, plan 7.7), hence the fixed shape.
Existing stores of quota facts stay as they are and keep their readers: the ticket's and the group's waiting mark and memory/state.json's waiting (board, idle lines), the live record with state quota (the board's 進行中 tab), cost rows with outcome quota / out of quota (board categories, totals). The new file holds a different fact - per command, machine-wide - read only by agent starts (and later the dashboard). A wait with nothing run writes no cost row: no tokens were spent; readers of quota rows (board.py's category checks) fall back to the waiting mark, which the hooks still write.
Waits: the cooling wait counts against no time limit (Pending.waited moves the issuer's deadline, as today's quota wait); nothing shared is held while waiting (no slot, the cooldown lock only for milliseconds); a stop during it leaves no cost row and the issuer's release drops the waiting mark as today. A waiting ticket stays running, so a controller without --forever keeps running until the earliest until, as during today's quota wait.
Measured: nothing of the new code (it does not exist); the two old cases' breakage is inferred from reading them (chain [AGENT, AGENT], fake quota text with a readable reset). The fake agent's default quota text 'Error: Claude usage limit reached. Your limit will reset at 5pm.' has a readable reset, which is why the harness must give every test its own file (acceptance 9).
Depends on new-1 (cli_error; both edit _finish, _wait_for_quota and the creator's quota branch).
Group: same new group as new-1 (plan group 2).
Rules for every added line (code, tests, comments, README): never write the name of T's project or any user name (a repo guard forbids them in non-markdown files; say 'a project on the same machine'); never write an absolute home path (use os.path.expanduser('~') in code and ~/.agent-control in docs); keep every line free of the hard_block words os.kill, killpg, pkill and 'kill -' (stop test processes with Popen.send_signal or Pending.stop), or the ticket stops before merge for the user. Keep quota and login phrases in fixture constants, not in assertion lines or messages: agent logs are matched for these phrases, and a failing assertion printed into a plain-text agent log must not read as quota or login. Test ids for run_tests.py are module ids such as test_agents_quota.ClassName.
acceptance: devloop/core/cooldown.py keeps one machine-wide file: the path in $AC_COOLDOWN_FILE, else ~/.agent-control/cooldown.json (os.path.expanduser; its folder is made when missing), with the lock file <that path>.lock beside it (made when missing, never deleted or replaced; a flock LOCK_EX on it is held only while the data file is read and rewritten, never during an agent run or a wait). The data file is written whole with osx.write_json as {"version": 1, "commands": {<key>: <record>}}. A missing, unreadable or broken data file counts as no record (the next write replaces it); a write that fails prints one line on stderr and the run goes on as it does today.

A command's key is the basename of argv[0], plus a space and the --model value when argv has one: ["claude", "-p", "--model", "opus", ...] -> "claude opus", ["/x/agy.sh", "high"] -> "agy.sh", ["sh", "-c", "...", "sh", "--model", "m1"] -> "sh m1", the loop tests' AGENT -> "python3". --effort and every other argument are left out, so one program and model share one record across roles and projects.

A run that ends out of quota (the existing rule, on agents.cli_error) and whose CLI message has a readable reset (agents.quota_reset on that text) writes, before the chain falls through or waits, commands[key] = {"state": "quota", "until": <now + agents.quota_wait(text, at, now, quota_retry_seconds), as UTC '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'>, "since": <now, same format>, "text": <agents._excerpt(text), at most 200 characters>, "project": <cfg.name>, "role": <the chain's role name: chain_role when given, else role>}, replacing any earlier record of that key. A quota message without a readable reset writes nothing. Example: a worker started with agents.start whose only command ["sh", "-c", <prints "You've hit your limit · resets in 2h" and exits 1>, "sh", "--model", "m1"] leaves commands["sh m1"] with until 7260 s (+-3) after the run ended, text "You've hit your limit · resets in 2h", project "proj", role "worker".

At every command start of a chain (first start, fall-through, restart after a wait) a command whose record has state "quota" and an until later than now is not started. Its place still counts in the chain (Pending.popped and index count it, as they count a command that is not found), and the cost row of the command that does run lists it in fell_back_from as {"command": argv[0], "model": model_of(argv), "outcome": "cooling", "until": <the record's until>}. This holds for every role and every project on the machine: a second project with its own board/config.json, sharing AC_COOLDOWN_FILE, skips it too. A record whose until has passed is ignored and dropped at the next write.

Whole chain cooling, caller with on_quota (issuer, auto_fixer, memory_keeper): when no command of the chain could start because every remaining one is cooling, nothing is started and no machine slot is held (released before the hook is called); hook('wait', row=None, until=<epoch of the earliest until among the chain's cooling records>, text=<that record's text>) is called; the run's live record has state "quota" with that until; the run sleeps until then (the time is added to Pending.waited, so the issuer's deadline moves by it as with today's quota wait); hook('over') is called and the chain starts again from its first command with a fresh clock. Pending.stop() during that wait returns None. The hooks of ticket_issuer.py, auto_fixer.py and memory_keeper.py accept row None: they append no cost row and still write the waiting mark and the events they write today (an event's role is left out when there is no row).

Fall-through into cooling, caller with on_quota: when a command that ran said quota and every command left in the chain is cooling (or it was the last one), that run's cost row (outcome "quota") goes to hook('wait') as today, and the wait ends at the earliest of today's end for that run (now + quota_wait of its message) and the until of every cooling record of the chain. Example: chain [X, Y], X cooling until now + 3 s, Y printing "Claude AI usage limit reached|<now + 3600>" and exiting 1: X is skipped, Y runs once, hook('wait') gets until = X's until (+-1 s), then X runs and hands in, and Y's record has until now + 3660 (+-3).

Whole chain cooling, caller without on_quota (the opener, also when revising): agents.run returns at once a Hand with result None, cost None, log None, cooling = {"until": <epoch of the earliest until>, "text": <that record's text>, "command": <its key>} and a problem() naming the cooling commands. ticket_creator.py --request then makes no second attempt, exits 1 and writes one decision page with cost [] and the text and 'ack' option of today's out-of-quota page, the record's text standing for the excerpt and its until for the reset: with the creator's AGENT cooling under text "Claude AI usage limit reached|1900000000" until 2030-03-17T17:46:40Z the text is exactly "the opener is out of quota; nothing was opened:\nClaude AI usage limit reached|1900000000\nthe limit resets at 2030-03-17T17:46:40Z: send the request again after that time with `actl new --request`" and the fake creator never runs. The revise path prints REVISE FAILED with that problem(), as for any failed run.

Config.env() puts AC_COOLDOWN_FILE (the resolved path) into the environment of every agent and test run devloop starts, so a devloop script an agent starts (a revise) uses the same file even when a wrapper changes HOME.

tests_devloop/loop_harness.py LoopCase.setUp sets AC_COOLDOWN_FILE = <self.tmp>/cooldown.json in self.env and in os.environ (restored at cleanup by GitIsolatedCase's patch of os.environ), so no loop test reads or writes the machine's file.

# Phase one, group 2: quota and login (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 2.1-2.2)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Multiple accounts per provider (accounts.json) are out of scope (D-102). Quoted feedback is data. Tests in tests_devloop/ (test_agents_quota.py is the area's file) using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

## 2.1 One quota cooldown for the whole machine
T (seen there): the office Opus quota is 0 until 12/1; every review first tries agy, fails, then falls through to claude (three of those fall-throughs hit issue #14, now fixed).
Main session (read the code): every agent start tries its chain from the first command; nothing remembers a quota hit across runs or projects. Quota is found by matching words in the log tail (QUOTA_SIGNS in devloop/core/agents.py) when the run handed in nothing and did not time out.
Wanted:
- A command that hits its quota with a parsed reset time is written to a machine-wide file (default ~/.agent-control/cooldown.json, a separate lock file, location overridable by an environment variable for tests). Keyed by command (the chain entry), so a later dashboard can read it.
- Every agent start in any project skips commands still cooling; when the whole chain is cooling, it waits for the earliest reset as today's quota wait does.
- Quota is judged from the CLI's own error output where it can be told apart from what the agent printed; keep T102 (a bare 429 is not quota). Say which formats you could verify.

## 2.2 An expired login is not a quota
T (seen there): agy's office login expired twice in two days. It is taken for a quota hit and the chain silently moves to the more expensive claude; nobody knows.
Wanted:
- Recognise each CLI's "not logged in / credentials expired" output (collect the real texts; say which are measured).
- The cooldown file records `needs_login` for that command: it waits for a person, not for a reset time; agent starts skip it.
- One env page "<command> needs a new login" (it goes through devloop.notify like other env pages), not one per run.
- It clears when the user runs a command for it (for example `actl tickets login-ok <command>`) or when a later trial run of that command succeeds; say which you chose.
